subject: Kim Hammer

actors.statutoryRelationship: Statewide election policy, training, and support; coordinates with State Board of Election Commissioners on rules and guidance.
Primary county election administrator; implements precincts, polling sites, early voting locations, absentee processes, and ballot logistics.
County-level governance body for election administration; subject to oath, duty, and compensation changes in Hammer-sponsored bills.
County funding and appropriation authority; bears indirect cost when election duties expand without state appropriation.

burdenThemes.plainEnglish: Shifts how precinct boundaries, polling sites, and vote centers are established or altered—more statutory process for county officials and commissioners.
burdenThemes.kellyContrastFrame: Kelly: modernize with county input and SOS playbooks—don't relocate voting by friction. Fund GIS/site review and public notice.
burdenThemes.debateUse: When Hammer claims 'local control,' ask who pays for remapping, notice, and voter confusion after site changes.

burdenThemes.plainEnglish: 2021 oath and governance changes for county election boards; 2023 co-sponsored compensation and duty amendments.
burdenThemes.kellyContrastFrame: Respect commissioners but give them training dollars and clear SOS guidance—not more liability without resources.
burdenThemes.debateUse: Rural counties with part-time boards: unfunded duty creep is a kitchen-table issue.

burdenThemes.plainEnglish: 2025 act amends county clerk designation of early voting locations (verify text for constraints vs. discretion).
burdenThemes.kellyContrastFrame: Expand convenient early voting where clerks and voters agree; SOS helps site planning.
burdenThemes.debateUse: Pair with voter-access frame, not fraud frame.

burdenThemes.plainEnglish: Poll watcher bill of rights and procedure changes add training and dispute surface at county polling places.
burdenThemes.kellyContrastFrame: Transparent observation yes; intimidation and clerk disruption no—SOS trains uniform standards.
burdenThemes.debateUse: Clerks as protagonists: 'don't turn our poll workers into referees without a rulebook.'

burdenThemes.plainEnglish: 2021 absentee amendments plus 2023 co-sponsored method/drop-box restrictions increase clerk procedure burden.
burdenThemes.kellyContrastFrame: Protect ballot chain-of-custody with staffing and secure drop-off options clerks can administer.
burdenThemes.debateUse: Seniors, shift workers, rural voters—access vs. paperwork.

burdenThemes.plainEnglish: Hotline and integrity-review concepts route complaints into systems counties and SBEC must respond to.
burdenThemes.kellyContrastFrame: Investigate real violations quickly; don't flood clerks with bad-faith dockets.

strategicBriefing.howToMessage: County modernization means clerks and election commissioners can execute consistent, voter-friendly processes—not absorb endless unfunded checklists from the Capitol.
strategicBriefing.debateImpact: Flips 'integrity' bills into workforce and budget stories quorum courts understand.
strategicBriefing.whenToUse: County elected officials, NASCE/clerks associations, regional papers, and debate segments on local government.
strategicBriefing.whenNotToUse: When only bill titles are known—verify operational clauses before claiming specific dollar costs.
strategicBriefing.oppositionSetup: Hammer: clerks wanted clarity; state must prevent chaos. Counter with partnership and resources.
strategicBriefing.kellyMessageHelp: Kelly as SOS: training portals, help desk, model policies, and defending counties when rules are ambiguous.
strategicBriefing.campaignAlignment: CountyWorkbench lane, rural access, election-administration competence.

governanceNotes: Burden dollar estimates are INTERPRETATION until fiscal impact statements or clerk surveys are attached.
Actor descriptions reflect Arkansas election law structure; confirm statutory citations in act-text pass.
